title: Modeling Preference Dependencies with Directed Acyclic Graphs for Narrative-Driven Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2610.37280v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Narrative-driven recommendation allows users to express multifaceted needs through free-form text where stated preferences naturally qualify and condition one another. Existing methods typically treat narratives as flat keyword combinations or unconstrained generative queries, failing to capture how complex preferences hierarchically refine and contextualize each other. We propose the Preference Dependency Graph Framework (PDG-F), a narrative-driven recommendation framework centered on explicit preference dependencies. Specifically, PDG-A (PDG-Agent) first parses unstructured requests to organize user preferences and their mutual qualifications into a directed acyclic Preference Dependency Graph (PDG). Through this graph, candidate evidence from the open Web is acquired via directed path retrieval, and final recommendations are determined by topological path ranking. translated_title: 基于有向无环图建模偏好依赖的叙事驱动推荐
translated_abstract: 叙事驱动推荐允许用户通过自由文本表达多方面的需求，其中所陈述的偏好之间自然地相互限定和制约。现有方法通常将叙事视为扁平的关键词组合或无约束的生成式查询，无法捕捉复杂偏好如何以层级方式相互细化并赋予语境。我们提出了偏好依赖图框架（PDG-F），这是一个以显式偏好依赖为核心的叙事驱动推荐框架。具体而言，PDG-A（PDG智能体）首先解析非结构化请求，将用户偏好及其相互之间的限定关系组织成有向无环的偏好依赖图（PDG）。通过该图，经由有向路径检索从开放网络获取候选证据，最终推荐由拓扑路径排序确定。在三个涵盖英语等多种场景的多样化领域上进行了全面的实验……
tldr: 提出偏好依赖图框架（PDG-F），利用有向无环图显式建模用户叙事中偏好之间的层级依赖关系，并通过有向路径检索和拓扑路径排序实现叙事驱动的推荐。
